Dr Jeremy Barnett,
Emergency Registrar
Maroubra Hospital
Lakes Road
Maroubra
1/6/2011
Dear Dr. Barnett,
RE: Mr. John ElvinDOB: 1963
Thank you for seeing Mr. Elvin, a 48- year old patient whose features are suggestive of anterior AMI and asthma exacerbation.
Mr. Elvin has a medical history of bronchial asthma and infrequent chest pain during exertion.  He is on regular medications of Seretide and salbutamol puffs. Moreover, he is smoker and alcohol dependent, but not interested in changing.
On 5/5/2011, Mr. Elvin was provisionally diagnosed as early stage of IHD. One week later, he was still complaining of chest pain on exertion and asthma progression related to upper airway inflammation. Mild wheeze and mild ischemic changes were detected. The patient commenced Lipitor for high cholesterol, nitrates, aspirin and arginine.
On 26/5/2011, the patient presented with the same manifestations as he was not compliant to the medications. I notified him about the value of anti- asthma preventive medications. I also advised him to have a reminder for all his medications, and to use salbutamol until asthma subsides.
Today, Mr. Elvin was presented with suspected anterior AMI and acute exacerbation of bronchial asthma. The initial management was commenced including oxygen mask, GTN patch, morphine, ibratropium bromide neubilizer and frusemide.
In view of the above, I am referring this patient for further management.
For any queries, please contact me  
Yours sincerely,
Doctor
